title: The four faces: “the face of an ox”, or “the face of a cherub”?
summary: Ezekiel 1:10 lists the four faces as a man, a lion, an ox and an eagle. Ezekiel 10:14 lists them as a cherub, a man, a lion and an eagle. Ezekiel 10:20 says of the creatures of the first vision “I knew that they were the cherubims”.
text: KJV Ezekiel 1:10: “they four had the face of an ox on the left side”. KJV Ezekiel 10:14: “the first face was the face of a cherub”. KJV Ezekiel 10:20: “I knew that they were the cherubims”.
reasoning: The two lists have the same four-fold shape and three of the same faces. Where 1:10 has “the face of an ox”, 10:14 has “the face of a cherub”, and no ox is named in 10:14. Verse 10:20 says the prophet knew the creatures were cherubim. The two lists can both stand if “cherub” is the name of the creature as a whole, or a name for the ox face; the verses quoted do not say which, and do not report a change of faces between the visions.
